newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Perry urges Russian Duma to ratify START arms pact.
newsitem.headline: Perry urges Russian Duma to ratify START arms pact.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry on Thursday urged the Russian parliament to approve further deep cuts in nuclear arms, but U.S. and Russian officials said he apparently did little to reverse opposition in two hours of hostile questioning from legislators.

Perry pressed members of the State Duma, the lower house of parliament, to ratify the Start-2 nuclear arms reduction treaty already approved by the U.S. Senate. Start-2 would slash U.S. and Russian nucear warheads to a third of their Cold War levels.
"Ratification of START-2 is quite problematic, it is not in the interest of the Russian side," Duma defence committee chairman Lev Rokhlin told Perry.
Pentagon spokesman Ken Bacon told reporters after the meeting that there was a lot of suspicion. "This (convincing the Duma) is going to be an uphill fight. There is no doubt about it," he said.

Perry told reporters after the closed session that it was "an excellent and productive discussion" on START-2, which would cut U.S. and Russian strategic nuclear arsenals to about 3,000 warheads on each side by 2003. Each now has over 6,000 such warheads.

But a number of Russian legislators, including communist Gennady Zyuganov, voiced continuing suspicion of START-2 and reiterated fierce opposition to planned expansion by NATO into Eastern Europe. Perry insisted the two issues were not linked.
